text:
maya: Quick follow-up from the RFC thread — I prototyped a tiny 'staging gateway' that sits in front of runtime pools and routes by precision profile/version. Goal: let us shadow and canary FP8/INT8/4bit artifacts per-tenant without touching prod routes. Thoughts on safety gates and required runtime checks?

sam: How does the gateway verify artifact compatibility? does it read model metadata + profile signatures, or do we rely on the runtime to reject mismatches?

liam: Perf numbers to keep in mind: on our p4d-like infra, fp8->int8 gives ~1.6x tokens/sec, 4-bit ~2.7x. Calibration step is offline but an extra latency on rollout if re-quant required. For 99p latency SLOs, we need to prevent large batch shifts when canary traffic is live.

jess: Ops perspective: +1 for gateway. My proposal: route types = shadow | canary | active; match on header X-Precision-Profile. Canaries get a qps cap + automatic rollback if "degradation" alarm trips. Will own runbook.

maya: Implementation notes I sketched: gateway should: 1) validate profile signature against model artifact (metadata key: precision.profile.v1), 2) apply per-tenant allowlist for experimental profiles, 3) attach provenance headers to downstream (X-Profile-Source, X-Profile-Version), 4) have a fallback policy (fallback_backend: float32).

sam: For the metadata checks: let's standardize keys and an enum for 'format' (fp8, int8, int4, fp16). Also include a small checksum for the quant table to avoid silent mismatch. If mismatch -> gateway responds 409 or reroutes to fallback backend with a decorated reason header.

liam: Runtime hook idea: when gateway switches a request from one precision lane to another, emit a KV-cache-invalidation hint so runtime can either rekey or force a cold start. Avoids cross-precision cache poisoning. Something like: `X-KV-Invalidate: true` on switch.

arjun: Telemetry + quality: we need per-token degscore + sample set comparisons for canary. Suggest windows: 1m latency histogram, 5m rolling degscore, and a shadow sampling stream (2% by default) to compute quality deltas against canonical outputs. If > threshold for N prompts, auto-fail canary. Also capture prompt hashes used for audits.

jess: Runbook checklist I'm adding: 1) enable shadow for tenant, 2) smoke prompts, 3) watch degscore and latency, 4) escalate to owner if hit thresholds, 5) auto rollback policy. I'll post a playable checklist.

maya: On fallback policies: I want a 'quality escrow' flag too — traffic held in escrow until a validation job completes (batch eval + sample freshness). Escrowed requests return 202 and queued; normal traffic kept hitting active backend. Useful for large tenant cutovers.

sam: Agree on fallback default = float32. Also let's add opt-in header for customers who want to accept best-effort low-bit (X-Allow-Lowbit: true) — otherwise they get strict compatibility enforcement.

liam: Small nit: batching behavior across lanes — gateway must avoid merging requests for different quant lanes into same batch. Either separate batch queues or insert guard tokens. Otherwise perf unpredictable.

arjun: Observability: add tags: profile_version, profile_source, fallback_reason, degscore_delta. Wire these into console dashboards so SRE/SE can filter per-tenant canary regressions.

maya: I pushed a prototype config for the gateway; pseudo-YAML below for clarity:

```
routes:
  - name: canary
    match: header X-Precision-Profile == \"fp8-v2-canary\"
    backend: ml-canary-01
    qps_limit: 50
    quality_escrow: false
  - name: shadow
    match: header X-Precision-Profile == \"fp8-shadow\"
    backend: ml-shadow-01
    sampling: 0.02
fallback:
  backend: ml-fp32-01
  policy: strict
```

jess: Nice. I'll wire the qps_limit to our quota system and add throttling rules. Can we also gate by region? some regions on-prem don't support int4 kernels yet.

maya: Good call — add region allowlist in profile metadata and gateway will validate region_before_routing.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: staged deploy started — staging-gateway v0.3 -> staging cluster. CI: unit+integration passes.

jess: I'll monitor the deploy. tagging owners: @maya @liam for smoke verification. :rocket:

liam: I'll run the perf microbench and post numbers to the thread. Also will add a short note about cache semantics for each quant lane.

arjun: I'll add the degscore alert rules and shadow sampling dashboard. Plan: initial canaries for internal tenants only, then expand. :eyes:
